summary: Bryan J. Cuevas is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Emory University under Donald Phillip Verene and earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins and David Germano, later serving as professor at Florida State University.

Bryan W. Van Norden specializes in philosophy and Sinology. He studied at Stanford University from circa 1985 to 1991 and became a professor in philosophy and Chinese & Japanese at Vassar College around 1996.
Bryce Ryan (1911–2002) worked in Indology and other fields. He held academic posts at Cornell University and the University of Peradeniya, where he taught Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah.

Bulcsu Siklós specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of London, studying under Charles R. Bawden and doctoral supervisor Tadeusz Skorupski, and held a post at SOAS University of London attested in 1996.

Bunga Fukui (1934–2017) studied Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He completed degrees at Waseda University and studied at École Pratique des Hautes Études under Paul Demiéville, Maxime Kaltenmark, and Rolf A. Stein, later serving as professor at Waseda University (~1978–2004).

Bunkyo Aoki (1886–1956) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. A disciple of Kōzui Ōtani who studied at Ryukoku University, he succeeded Tokan Tada as a Tibetan language lecturer at the University of Tokyo in 1951.

Bunsaku Kurata (1918–1983) worked in archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology after studying at Aoyama Gakuin and Waseda University. He held positions at the National Commission for Protection of Cultural Properties, Tokyo National Museum, and served as Director of Nara National Museum (1975).

Bunyiu Nanjio (1849–1927) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology. Educated at Otani University and Oxford under Friedrich Max Müller and Arthur Anthony Macdonell, he held posts at the University of Tokyo and served as director of Otani University.

Bunzaburo Matsumoto (1869–1944) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy who studied at the University of Tokyo. He taught at Rikkyo University and the First Higher School before serving as professor of Indian philosophy at Kyoto University (1906–1929).

Burchard Brentjes (1929–2012) worked in archaeology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg under Heinz Mode, whom he later succeeded in 1978 during his tenure there (~1954–1980).

Burkhard Quessel specializes in Tibetology and Indology. He studied at the University of Hamburg, where he was attested as a member in 1997, and later served as a curator at the British Library (attested 2002–2012).

Burton Stein (1926–1996) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He held academic posts at the University of Hawaiʻi from circa 1968 to 1984 and at SOAS University of London from circa 1984 to 1996.

Burton Watson (1925–2017) was a scholar of Sinology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his BA and PhD at Columbia University and studied at Kyoto University, later holding posts at Kyoto, Doshisha, Columbia, and Stanford University.

C. D. Sebastian works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He completed his PhD at Banaras Hindu University, studied under mentors including Paul Williams and Gavin D'Costa, and served as Professor of Indian Philosophy at IIT Bombay (attested 2016).

C. Kunhan Raja (1895–1963) was an Indologist who served as Head of the Department of Sanskrit at the University of Madras, with tenures recorded in 1927 and 1946. His students included K. Kunjunni Raja, Madhav Krishna Sharma, and H. G. Narahari.
C. R. Krishnamacharlu (b. 1888) was a scholar in the fields of history, archaeology, and Indology. He pursued his education at Madras Christian College and Pachaiyappa's College.

C. S. Srinivasachari (1890–1951) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. Over his career, he held posts as a professor at Pachaiyappa's College and at Annamalai University (attested 1932–1933).
C. S. Sundaram was an Indologist who taught at Madras Sanskrit College and served as Reader in Sanskrit at the University of Madras in 1951. He also taught Tomy Augustine.

C. W. Huntington, Jr. (1949–2020) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan (~1978–1986) under Luis O. Gómez and Madhav M. Deshpande, and was a professor at Hartwick College (~1993–2020).

Calambur Sivaramamurti (1910–1983) studied Indology and archaeology under S. Kuppuswami Sastri at Presidency College, Chennai. He held curatorial posts at the Government Museum, Chennai, the Archaeological Survey of India at the Indian Museum, and the National Museum, New Delhi.
